_comment: Status-tint ratchet ceiling — the count of inline `color-mix(` occurrences under web/src/pages, measured by countInlineColorMix() in statusTint.test.ts. It may only SHRINK: a new hand-rolled tint turns CI red, and each migration to ui/StatusPill lowers this number IN THE SAME COMMIT. Keep it at the measured actual and BRACKET rather than assume — a ceiling of 177 fails with 'expected 178 to be less than or equal to 177', so the live count is exactly 178. Slack is not a safety margin here, it is a hole: one unit of it lands the next new inline tint green and unrecorded (`primitiveAdoption.baseline.json` records that hole absorbing a real regression). 179 -> 178 (bugfix-stale-search-binding): settings/SearchPanel.tsx's provider-state chip needed a THIRD state, `not installed`, and the row hand-rolled the 16% tint + ink pair twice; both toned states now ride the primitive, so the file went 2 -> 0 while gaining a state. `not configured` stayed a local span on purpose — a solid surface fill is a neutral GROUND, not a tone tint, which is the same split settings/bento.tsx draws and design/primitiveShadowing.test.ts pins. The remaining SearchPanel mix is the selected row's 12% primary fill, a selection ground this ratchet's own header names as legitimately non-pill. 178 -> 177: three hand-rolled 10% tints landed after that (the agent's unavailable-model note, its hooks-waiting note, and the attachment chip, whose inline style only repeated its own `bg-primary/10`), taking the live count to 180. All three moved to the theme's toned-fill utilities (`bg-warn/10`, `bg-primary/10`), which paint the same 10% of the same semantic token and which the pages already use for exactly this; none of the three is a pill, so StatusPill was not the home. Bracketed again: a ceiling of 176 fails with 'expected 177 to be less than or equal to 176'. 177 -> 179 (improvement-home-overview-shows-your-agents-now-and-next): Home's agents band draws each agent's done and working time as bars on a time track, a 38% quiet and a 60% active state fill over the surface. A bar on a track is a genuinely non-pill fill, not a status label, so StatusPill is not its home, and the theme has no toned-fill utility for the state tokens. 179 -> 181 (the same band, the owner's pick of its variations): the rows that wait on you and the rows that failed today sit on top, each on a 9% ground of its state token over the band's surface (waiting and blocked, one each). A row's ground is not a status label, so StatusPill is not its home. The theme's toned fills bg-warn/10 and bg-danger/10 name the same colours today, since state-waiting and state-blocked are aliases of warn and danger; the band names the state tokens instead, as its marks and dots do, so a state re-pointed in tokens.css layer 2 takes its ground with it. The mix goes into the surface, so the ground is opaque, and the track's ‘← before’ label painted on it hides the baseline behind it, which a translucent bg-warn/10 could not. Those tokens sit in :root, not @theme, so no bg-state-* utility exists. Bracketed: a ceiling of 180 fails with 'expected 181 to be less than or equal to 180'.
